deviation_mechanism: The R1 configuration used uniform 100.0 nm layers across all 12 positions, likely coinciding with a constructive interference condition for the target bandwidth, yielding the historical peak of 0.9275. Subsequent optimization steps altered critical thicknesses (e.g., R4 candidate layer 6 expanded to 168.06 nm, layer 8 thinned to 29.09 nm, layer 10 to 31.14 nm). These physical deviations changed optical path lengths (ΔL = 2nd), shifting phase accumulation and converting previously constructive interference into destructive interference within the 420-700 nm band. The deterministic search pushed the stack into a local optical minimum where modified layer ratios disrupt the intended broadband transmission profile, trapping the solver and preventing score recovery.
continue_rationale: The route exhibits clear degradation from its initial optimum rather than convergence to a physical performance ceiling. Scores plateaus between 0.7689 (R5) and 0.8160 (R4) indicate entrapment in a sub-optimal design basin, not exhaustion of beneficial parameter space. Continuing enables a targeted initialization repair to escape the current local minimum and attempt to reclaim the high-transmittance regime observed in R1.
insight_for_next: Implement a multi-start stochastic initialization for the next round: seed 50% of the candidate pool at the proven R1 uniform 100.0 nm baseline to anchor the search, and seed the other 50% with deliberately phase-shifted quartet patterns (alternating 50.0/150.0 nm pairs) to explicitly probe adjacent constructive interference peaks. Pair this with a population-based optimizer (e.g., Differential Evolution) to force structural diversification and prevent deterministic drift into the current destructive-interference valley.
